fields.why: Rates are reported and ranked across 6 age groups, 4 race/ethnicity groups, SES quartiles (housing problems, income inequality, unemployment) and 6 urbanicity levels.
Sex has only 2 levels; county urbanicity is framed alongside area SES as a social-position stratifier of persons' injuries, not an outbreak location.

The only inference is RR (year vs 2019) CIs within each level; group differences in rates and in RRs ('highest', 'largest increases') are only set side by side. Mechanical flag is a false alarm: the tests are period contrasts stratified by SPD, not tests across SPD levels, so rule 2 does not apply.

brief_issues: Rule 6's 'Rule 2 governs whenever a test is reported per SPD level' could be read to cover a within-level test of a non-SPD contrast (here year vs 2019); the brief could say rule 2 applies only when the SPD is a margin of the test.
